name: 047_tv_super_scalper_tf1
hypothesis: TradingView port T4 (PLAN.md section 13) from the Pine v5 source the owner supplied: 'Super Scalper - 5 Min 15 Min'. The author's claim: a bar whose body exceeds one WMA-ATR is an impulse, and taking it in the direction of the RSI trend (RSI 25 above RSI 100 for longs, below for shorts) catches the continuation. Counterparty: traders fading a strong bar. Author defaults kept: ATR 14 with WMA smoothing, multiplier 1.0, RSI 25 / 100, source chart 15m (the author's own timeframe). The EMA 21/65 'golden cross' is only plotted in the script and is not part of the entry. DEVIATIONS: (1) the script computes a stop (2 ATR beyond the signal bar's low/high) and a take-profit (5 ATR beyond its high/low) but never passes them to an order - on TradingView it only exits by reversing on the opposite signal. The engine must have a stop, so the author's own numbers are used: stop = the signal bar's low (high) minus (plus) 2 ATR (swing stop, n 1, buffer 2 ATR, unclamped), take-profit = 5 ATR from the entry (the author measured it from the bar's high/low); (2) a time stop is added because the engine has no stop-and-reverse; it is the only grid key; (3) TradingView's default commission is 0, here 0.05% taker + 0.02% slippage + funding. Variants in chart mode (same bar counts, ATR exits unchanged). [Timeframe variant of 047_tv_super_scalper, 15m -> 1m, mode chart: same bar counts and ATR multiples, hold x0.0666667, pct stop x0.258.]
